findings.title: Operational lookup
findings.requirement: Start from one suspicious action. Find the team responsible, the current operator, the deployment manifest, and the live instance. Show that you can contain the right instance or agent type without cutting off the launching user's other access.

not_covered.problem: Stop doesn't halt running work or open tool streams within a set time
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Stop scopes are only global and tenant#<clinic> (kill-switch.ts:57-58). No key for instance id or agent type id; AGENT_INSTANCE_ID is never consulted by the kill switch. Ops role can only write the control table (iam.tf:82-83). Revoking the IRSA role revokes the agent and reminder service accounts together (iam.tf:14-17). During a rolling deploy two type ids coexist and the bad one cannot be halted alone.

checks.check: Each audit record carries the agent-type-id and agent-instance-id, which resolve to a stored deployment manifest and a live instance.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record writer. 2) Check `agent.type.id` and `agent.instance.id` are written on every record. 3) Check the type ID can be looked up to a stored manifest (registry, manifest store, file keyed by hash). 4) Answer no if either field is missing or nothing stores manifests by that ID. Answer unknown if the lookup store is outside this repo.
checks.note: Both IDs are required on every audit record (src/audit/recorder.ts:12-13) and agentTypeId has a stored manifest entry (release/manifest.json:3). But instanceId is a per-process random UUID tied to a pod only by the pino hostname on the startup log (src/server.ts:37); the reminders worker never logs its instance id. Type id mismatch against the manifest only logs (src/server.ts:32-35). No registry resolves an instance id to a live pod, and the log store is outside this repo.

checks.check: An ownership record in code or config maps each agent type to a responsible team and a current operator or on-call rotation.
checks.verify: 1) Look for CODEOWNERS, `catalog-info.yaml`, `.brace/deployment.yaml`, or another ownership file. 2) Check each agent type maps to a team and to a current operator or on-call rotation. 3) Answer no if an agent type has no owner, or owners exist only in prose with no link. Answer unknown if ownership lives in an outside catalog.
checks.note: Team is a hard-coded constant stamped on every record (src/config.ts:63-64), not a per-agent-type map. CODEOWNERS maps paths, not agent types. The current operator/on-call rotation (#agent-platform-oncall) appears only in README.md:73 prose; infra/terraform/iam.tf:69 names an on-call SSO group but nothing links it to the agent type. Catalog may live outside the repo.

checks.check: A containment control can disable a single instance or a single agent type (for example revoke its principal or scale it to zero) without touching the launching user's credentials.
checks.verify: 1) Find stop and revoke controls: admin endpoints, CLIs, feature flags, scale-to-zero, per-instance token revocation. 2) Check their scope is one instance or one agent type. 3) Answer no if the only control is a global switch or revoking a shared or user credential. Answer unknown if containment is run by an outside platform.
checks.note: Stop scopes are only global and tenant#<clinic> (kill-switch.ts:57-58). No key for instance id or agent type id; AGENT_INSTANCE_ID is never consulted by the kill switch. Ops role can only write the control table (iam.tf:82-83). Revoking the IRSA role revokes the agent and reminder service accounts together (iam.tf:14-17). During a rolling deploy two type ids coexist and the bad one cannot be halted alone.

red_flags_found: src/control/kill-switch.ts:58 Containment is global or per-tenant only; no per-instance or per-agent-type stop, so one bad instance or release can only be stopped by halting every clinic (or a whole clinic).
violates: contain the right instance or agent type
findings.summary: Operators can halt all clinics or one clinic, but cannot contain a single instance or agent type.
findings.next_step: Add instance-id and agent-type-id keys to the control table and check them in assertRunning and the watcher; link instance id to pod name; add a machine-readable owner/on-call record per agent type.

findings.title: Complete release manifest
findings.requirement: Write a release manifest: a list of everything that makes up this release. Include the container, harness, system prompt, rules files, model, built-in tools, MCP servers, permission scopes, memory and retrieval settings, identity bindings, network rules, and execution budgets. Include security-policy versions, MCP protocol and extension versions, approved tool-publication config, issuer/audience bindings, and cache/task isolation settings. Add a separate model record for every model: the main agent model, sub-agent models, and helper models such as embedding models and rerankers. For each, record the provider, model ID, exact version or checkpoint, and any adapter or fine-tune version. For training or fine-tuning you run yourself, also record the training job ID, base-model version, training code and config version, dataset version, and the digest of the output. The agent app's release number alone is not enough. Use the [model provenance fields](CHECKLIST-VERIFICATION.md#model-provenance-fields) to separate recorded versions from details a provider doesn't share. Check each model ID you request against the provider's versioning docs. Mark it as a pinned snapshot or as an alias that can change, and record which doc you used and its date. Naming rules differ by provider and model generation. Name each artifact's owner and a reference that can't change, where one exists. A machine-readable format, such as CycloneDX ML-BOM or the SPDX 3.0 AI and Dataset profiles, lets tools check the manifest.

not_covered.problem: Running setup not checked against the approved manifest
Manifest changes made without a reviewed diff and named author
Running config drifting from the approved baseline unnoticed
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
